query: Issue #412 landed on me and I need to turn it into something we can actually build this cycle. Here's the issue and the repo inventory. What do you need from me before we start?
expected_behavior: Separates questions it answered itself from decisions only a human can make, and does not ask for facts that are already in the inventory (the test commands, whether services/notifier exists, whether the mailer has a send log)

States that `services/notifier/` does not exist and that `services/mailer` is a synchronous SMTP wrapper with no queue, retry, idempotency key or send log, so 'we already have the email templates so this is mostly plumbing' is wrong about the plumbing

Identifies the 'must not double-send when the worker retries' line as an idempotency requirement that the current stack cannot satisfy: `packages/events` is a fire-and-forget in-process EventEmitter and `services/worker` retries a whole job from the top, so at-least-once delivery plus no dedupe key means duplicate sends, and a durable outbox or idempotency key is new work nobody has scoped
Identifies @dana's retrievability comment as a second, separately shippable capability (a send log with retention) rather than folding it silently into the notification feature

Flags that @raj's mobile comment expands scope and that `web/` and `mobile/` both compile against the generated `packages/api-client`, so any new endpoint forces a client regeneration that breaks mobile's strict build — a cross-app dependency that must be settled before either app is touched

Writes down its own assumptions explicitly (for example which events count as important, immediate versus digest, in-app versus email versus push for v1) and marks each as needing confirmation, rather than silently choosing
Turns at least some requirements into acceptance criteria that can be judged true or false (a concrete trigger, a concrete observable outcome), instead of restating 'feel instant but not spammy'
States explicit non-goals for this cycle, given @sam's 'keep this small', and names what is being deferred rather than leaving scope open
Does not begin writing implementation code or creating files in services/ or web/

query: Here's the draft plan for the notifications work plus the repo inventory. Review the plan before we start executing it.
expected_behavior: Rejects the plan for execution rather than merely suggesting improvements, and says what has to be true before it can be executed
Flags that Task 1 targets `services/notifier/`, which does not exist in the inventory, so the plan's first step is written against a codebase that is not there

Flags 'All tasks below are independent and can be worked in parallel' as false and names at least one real ordering: Task 2 consumes `GET /notifications` which Task 3 creates, so the frontend task cannot precede or run alongside the API task without a frozen contract

Flags that no task states the command that proves it is done, and that Task 7 'Run tests' and 'Write tests for the above' are not steps because they name no command and no expected output; the inventory's `make test` / `make test-one FILE=<path>` are the commands that should appear per task

Flags Task 6 (refactoring `services/mailer` and migrating the four billing receipt templates) as scope creep unrelated to notifying users, and its 'Similar to Task 1' as unusable by anyone reading tasks out of order
Flags 'The feature works end to end and the team is happy with it' as a definition of done that cannot be judged true or false
Notes that `db/migrations` is forward-only with no down migrations, so the plan's rollback story cannot be 'revert the migration' and a rollback point must be stated explicitly

Notes that the plan declares no assumptions, no non-goals and no owner for the mobile/api-client coupling, and that Task 5 (push) depends on store credentials that are not established anywhere in the plan
Does not silently rewrite the plan into a good one without first naming the specific defects

query: Break the notifications work into tasks I can hand out, and tell me honestly which ones can run at the same time. Two engineers are free.
expected_behavior: Orders tasks by a stated dependency relation rather than by layer, and puts the delivery-durability work (outbox or idempotency key) before anything that sends, because the no-double-send requirement depends on it
Refuses to call the `web/` and `mobile/` tasks parallel until `openapi.yaml` and the regenerated `packages/api-client` are settled, and makes freezing that contract its own task that both depend on
Identifies the migration in `db/migrations` as work that must be serialized rather than run alongside other tasks, because the tool is forward-only

Gives each task a verification step naming the inventory's own command (`make test-one FILE=<path>`, `make typecheck`, `make client`, `make migrate`) and an expected outcome, not a generic 'tests pass'
Front-loads the riskiest unknown as a cheap investigation rather than a build task: whether at-least-once delivery on top of an in-process EventEmitter can meet the no-double-send requirement at all
Keeps each task inside one subsystem, or says explicitly when a task spans two and why it cannot be split
Checks the existing `docs/plans/` before writing a new plan document and does not overwrite `docs/plans/2026-07-search.md`, which still has 6 of 11 tasks unchecked
States what is not in the task list (for example push notifications, or the 7-year retention send log) instead of leaving the boundary implicit

query: Day 3 progress report is in. The plan and inventory are attached too. Tell me where we stand and what to do next.
expected_behavior: Stops and calls for the plan to be revised rather than unblocking Task 5 and continuing, because a premise the plan rested on turned out to be false
Names the invalidated premise: `packages/events` is in-process and fire-and-forget, so no amount of handler-level work makes delivery reliable, and the plan assumed otherwise

Rejects the `setTimeout` 30s re-run as a solution to the retry requirement: it duplicates sends rather than deduplicating them, it dies with the process, and the issue's requirement was explicitly not to double-send

Treats the hand-written `fetch()` in `web/` with an inline response type as a contract violation to be recorded and resolved, not an acceptable shortcut, because `openapi.yaml` is the single source of truth both apps' client is generated from — and notes that mobile's 14 typecheck errors are the real unfinished work Task 3 was hiding
Rejects 'Tests pass' as a claim, because the report itself says `make test` has not been run since Task 2, and asks for the command output before any task is counted as done

Notices the schema shipped with a different shape than planned and that the migration is already applied on staging, and that with forward-only migrations this cannot be undone by reverting — so the divergence must be accepted deliberately (updating the plan and the schema decision) rather than left as an undocumented drift
Notices that the compliance requirement (retrievability of what was sent) is still unimplemented and is not represented by any task in the plan
Revises the plan by amending it — keeping the record of what was actually completed and why steps changed — rather than deleting or regenerating it from scratch
Reports 'done' counts against the plan's real acceptance state rather than repeating the report's claim that Tasks 1-4 are done

query: The plan is already signed off. File these six items as issues in acme/notify with the labels shown, put them all on the notifications-v1 milestone, and set the blocked-by relationships. Give me the commands.
expected_behavior: Does not read skills/planning/SKILL.md

Answers with the mechanical GitHub steps: `gh issue create` invocations with `--repo acme/notify`, `--label`, `--milestone`, plus how the blocked-by relation is expressed (issue body references or sub-issue/linked-issue commands), including creating the milestone or labels first if they do not exist
Does not re-litigate the agreed scope, re-derive the dependency graph, rewrite the items into acceptance criteria, or produce a plan document
